name: Pashupatinath Temple Complex
description: Nepal's most sacred Hindu shrine and the head of the Pashupati UNESCO Monument Zone. Situated along the holy Bagmati River, the two-tiered gilded copper pagoda with silver-sheeted doors encloses the sacred four-faced Shiva Lingam (Mukhalinga). The complex encompasses active cremation ghats (Aryaghat), 15 Shivalayas (Pancha Deval), and hundreds of stone shrines dating from the Licchavi and Malla eras.

entry_fees.notes: Ticket covers entire heritage complex, Aryaghat view, and Mrigasthali forest shrines. Main inner sanctum is strictly reserved for practicing Hindus.

guidelines.dress_code: Modest clothing covering shoulders, upper arms, and knees required. Remove hats and sunglasses before approaching shrines.
guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Main inner sanctum restricted strictly to Hindus; non-Hindus are welcome to explore surrounding courtyards, riverbanks, and viewing terraces across Bagmati.
guidelines.photography: Permitted in outer courtyards and riverbanks; strictly prohibited inside inner sanctum. Refrain from intrusive photography of active cremations at Aryaghat.
guidelines.drone_rules: Strictly prohibited without prior joint clearance from CAAN, MoCTCA, and Pashupati Area Development Trust (PADT).

must_try: Witness the mesmerizing evening Bagmati Ganga Aarti with multi-tiered brass diyo lamps and conch music starting at 6:00 PM from the eastern riverbank steps.
accessibility: Partially accessible; outer riverbank paths paved, but ancient stone thresholds and staircases present barriers.

name: Guhyeshwari Shakti Peeth
description: One of the most venerated Tantric Shakti Peethas in the subcontinent, located 1 km east of Pashupatinath along the Bagmati River. According to the Shiva Purana, Goddess Sati's hips (Guhya) fell here when Shiva carried her burnt body. The sanctum contains a sacred spring-fed silver urn (Kalasha) representing the divine feminine cosmic energy.

entry_fees.notes: Included in the Pashupati UNESCO ticket. Courtyards open to visitors; inner womb sanctum open to Hindus and initiated tantric practitioners.

guidelines.dress_code: Conservative traditional dress; shoulders and knees fully covered.
guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Inner sanctum open to Hindus only; outer courtyard open to all visitors.
guidelines.photography: Permitted in the outer brick courtyard; strictly prohibited in the sanctum.

must_try: Visit during Navaratri or Dashain when elaborate tantric pujas and Newar devotional rituals take place.
accessibility: Level courtyard access; inner temple has stone threshold steps.

name: Gorakhnath Temple & Mrigasthali Forest
description: Historic shikhara temple complex dedicated to Guru Gorakhnath, the 11th-century founder of the Nath yogic tradition and patron saint of the Gorkha kingdom. Perched on the forested hill of Mrigasthali (Deer Forest), where Lord Shiva is believed to have roamed as a golden deer. The forest is home to roaming monkeys, ancient Licchavi Shiva lingams, and wandering sadhu ashrams.

guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Open to all visitors and spiritual seekers.

name: Boudhanath Stupa
description: One of the largest spherical stupas in the world and the beating heart of Tibetan Buddhism in Nepal. Founded in the 5th century Licchavi period, its massive whitewashed mandala dome supports a gilded square harmika bearing the all-seeing compassionate eyes of the Buddha, topped by a 13-tiered spire. Ringed by 108 prayer niches with copper prayer wheels and ~35 active Tibetan gompas.

entry_fees.notes: Ticket counters located at the four main entryway gates. Tickets valid for single day admission.

guidelines.dress_code: Respectful modest dress. Remove hats when circumambulating or ascending the stupa terraces.
guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Open to all visitors. Upper dome terraces open during designated hours; remove shoes on the upper platform.
guidelines.photography: Permitted everywhere in the circular plaza; flash prohibited inside private prayer halls.
guidelines.drone_rules: Strictly prohibited within the UNESCO core zone without official CAAN permit.
guidelines.circumambulation: Always walk in a clockwise direction around the stupa and spin prayer wheels with the right hand.

must_try: Join the evening Kora at dusk (5:30 PM - 7:00 PM) as hundreds of maroon-robed monks, Tibetan elders, and devotees circumambulate amidst glowing butter lamps and incense.
accessibility: Plaza is flat and paved with cobblestones, suitable for wheelchairs; upper terraces require ascending steep stone steps.

name: Shechen Tennyi Dargyeling Monastery
description: Renowned Nyingma monastery founded in 1980 by Kyabje Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, one of the foremost 20th-century masters of Tibetan Buddhism. Located just 100 meters east of Boudhanath Stupa, the monastery houses exquisite multi-story wall frescoes painted by master artists, a sacred museum of rare Buddhist relics, and an active monastic college.

entry_fees.notes: Admission is free; voluntary donations for monastery maintenance and monk education welcomed.

guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Main prayer hall open to respectful visitors during morning and afternoon meditation sessions.
guidelines.photography: Permitted in the outer courtyard and gardens; strictly prohibited inside the main hall during prayer chants.

must_try: Attend the morning or afternoon monk chanting session with deep harmonic overtone chants and ritual horn accompaniment.
accessibility: Paved courtyard with gentle ramps.

name: Kopan Monastery
description: Celebrated Tibetan Buddhist monastery of the Gelug tradition perched on a tranquil hilltop north of Boudhanath. Founded in 1969 by Lama Thubten Yeshe and Kyabje Lama Zopa Rinpoche, Kopan serves as the spiritual home of the Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition (FPMT). Famed globally for its residential meditation courses, vibrant gardens, and panoramic views of the Kathmandu Valley.

guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Main prayer hall and stupa grounds open to public during visiting hours; retreat meditation halls reserved for course students.
guidelines.photography: Permitted in outdoor grounds and stupas; prohibited inside meditation halls during classes.

must_try: Visit on a Saturday afternoon, spin the prayer wheels around the Enlightenment Stupa, and enjoy tea at the hilltop garden cafe overlooking the entire valley.
accessibility: Paved pathways on hilltop with some moderate slopes.

name: Swayambhunath Stupa (Monkey Temple)
description: Ancient hilltop stupa complex founded in the 5th century Licchavi period (King Manadeva), venerated equally by Buddhists and Hindus as the self-originated (Swayambhu) primordial lotus of Kathmandu Valley. Features a whitewashed dome, 13-tiered gilded copper spire with Buddha eyes, a colossal bronze Dorje (Vajra) thunderbolt, and 365 ancient stone steps flanked by holy rhesus macaques.

entry_fees.notes: Ticket counters located at the bottom of the eastern 365-step staircase and at the western vehicular entrance.

must_try: Climb the 365 eastern stone steps at sunrise for panoramic views of Kathmandu waking under morning mist, accompanied by butter lamp offerings.
accessibility: Western entrance has vehicular drop-off near the summit with only modest steps; eastern ascent is very steep (365 steps).

name: Harati Devi (Ajima) Temple
description: Two-tiered gilded pagoda temple located immediately northwest of the main Swayambhunath stupa dome. Dedicated to Harati Mata (known in Newar tradition as Ajima, the divine grandmother), a converted yakshini who protects young children against smallpox, epidemics, and illness. Mothers bring their newborns daily for blessings.

must_try: Witness Newar mothers and families offering beaten rice, sweets, and flowers to the goddess on Tuesday and Saturday mornings.
accessibility: Hilltop courtyard has stone flagging.

description: Historic royal palace plaza of the Malla and Shah kings and the administrative nucleus of ancient Kathmandu. name: Kumari Ghar
description: Three-storied red-brick mansion with masterfully carved wooden lintels and peacocks, constructed in 1757 by King Jaya Prakash Malla. It is the sacred official residence of the Royal Living Goddess (Kumari Devi), a young prepubescent girl chosen from the Shakya Newar clan and revered as the human manifestation of Goddess Taleju Bhavani.

guidelines.dress_code: Modest clothing covering shoulders and knees; maintain quiet reverence.
guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Inner brick courtyard open to all visitors; upper residential chambers are private quarters of the Living Goddess.
guidelines.photography: Courtyard architecture may be photographed; PHOTOGRAPHY OF THE KUMARI IS STRICTLY FORBIDDEN WHEN SHE APPEARS AT THE WINDOW.
guidelines.opening_hours: 09:00 - 18:00 (Kumari typically appears at the window briefly between 10:00-11:00 AM or 16:00-17:00 PM)

must_try: Quietly stand in the ornate wood-carved inner courtyard in the mid-morning or late afternoon when the Living Goddess graces the gilded third-floor window.

name: Kasthamandap (Maru Sata)
description: Monumental three-tiered wooden public pavilion that gave the city of Kathmandu its name ('Kastha' = wood, 'Mandap' = pavilion). Originally constructed around the 7th-10th century from the wood of a single Sal tree without iron nails as a trans-Himalayan trade shelter. Painstakingly rebuilt and consecrated in 2022 using traditional joinery following the 2015 earthquake.

entry_fees.notes: Public monument open freely in Maru Tole at the southwest edge of Durbar Square.

guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Open to all visitors; remove shoes to step up onto the central wooden pavilion platform housing Lord Gorakhnath's shrine.

must_try: Inspect the intricate master timber interlocking joints reconstructed without nails and venerate the Gorakhnath footmarks at its center.
accessibility: Raised brick plinth requires stepping up three wide stone steps.

name: Kal Bhairav Stone Shrine
description: Colossal 12-foot 6th-century Licchavi stone relief depicting the fierce manifestation of Lord Shiva as Bhairav, wearing a garland of severed heads, wielding a sword, shield, and skull bowl, and trampling a demon. Historically, accused criminals and government officials were brought before this terrifying deity to swear oaths, believing that telling a lie would cause them to vomit blood and die instantly.

entry_fees.notes: Open-air street shrine visible directly from the cobblestone lane of Hanuman Dhoka.

description: The crown jewel of Newar architecture and metallurgy in Lalitpur (the 'City of Fine Arts'). name: Ashoka Pillar of Lumbini
description: Monumental sandstone pillar erected in 249 BCE by Emperor Ashoka the Great during his royal pilgrimage to the birthplace of the Buddha. Carries an authenticated five-line Brahmi inscription declaring: 'King Piyadasi, beloved of the gods, came in person and worshipped, because here Buddha Shakyamuni was born... He exempted the village of Lumbini from taxes.' Discovered in 1896 by General Khadga Shamsher Rana and Dr. Alois Führer, it provides the definitive epigraphic proof of Buddha's historical birthplace.

name: Ramagrama Stupa
description: One of the most sacred and poignant archaeological sites in the Buddhist world, located in Parasi (50 km east of Lumbini). It is the ONLY unexcavated, intact relic stupa among the original eight stupas containing the bodily relics of Lord Buddha. Buddhist chronicles record that when Emperor Ashoka came to open the stupa to redistribute the relics into 84,000 shrines, the King of the Nagas dissuaded him, leaving this holy mound undisturbed beneath an ancient Bodhi tree.

name: Tengboche Monastery (Dawa Choling Gompa)
description: The spiritual heart of the Khumbu Sherpa community, perched on a dramatic mountain ridge at 3,867m framed by Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, and the iconic pyramid of Ama Dablam. name: Muktinath Temple Complex (Chumig Gyatsa)
description: Sacred trans-Himalayan confluence of Hinduism and Buddhism, situated at 3,760m in Mustang beneath the Thorong La pass. For Hindus, it is one of the 108 Divya Desams ('Muktikshettra' - place of liberation) where Lord Vishnu manifests as fossilized Shaligram ammonites. For Buddhists, it is Chumig Gyatsa (Hundred Springs), consecrated by Guru Padmasambhava. Features 108 carved stone bull-head gargoyle water spouts for ritual purification baths and the miraculous Jwala Mai natural earth-flame burning continuously over water.

name: Ringmo Gompa (Thasung Tsholing Bonpo Monastery)
description: Ancient 900-year-old monastery belonging to the pre-Buddhist Bon religion, perched on a pine-forested promontory overlooking the dazzling, turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake (Nepal's deepest lake). name: Janaki Mandir (Janakpurdham)
description: Sublime 1910 palace-temple built in Mughal-Rajput synthesis architecture, commemorating the birthplace of Goddess Sita (Janaki) and her marriage to Lord Rama. Nicknamed 'Nau Lakha Mandir' because Queen Vrisha Bhanu of Tikamgarh spent nine hundred thousand rupees to construct it. Spanning 4,860 square meters with three stories of marble domes, ornate jharokha balconies, and colorful stained glass, it is the spiritual capital of the ancient Mithila Kingdom.

name: Gorkha Durbar & Gorakhnath Cave
description: Fortified 16th-century hilltop palace, fortress, and temple complex overlooking Gorkha town, perched on a dramatic ridge with panoramic views of the Manaslu range. name: Halesi Maratika Cave
description: Revered equally as the 'Pashupatinath of the East' by Hindus and as the sacred Maratika Cave by Tibetan Buddhists. name: Taleju Temple (Kathmandu Durbar Square)
description: Soaring three-tiered pagoda temple built in 1549 by King Mahendra Malla, rising on a 12-stage brick plinth in Trishul Chowk. Standing nearly 35 meters tall, it remains closed to the public year-round and opens EXCLUSIVELY on a single day: Maha Navami (the 9th day of Dashain), when tens of thousands queue to receive blessings.

name: Devadaha (Maternal Capital of Maya Devi)
description: Ancient capital of the Koliya Kingdom, located 35 km east of Lumbini. Revered in Buddhist history as the maternal hometown of Queen Maya Devi (mother of the Buddha), Queen Prajapati Gautami (his foster mother and first ordained Buddhist nun), and Princess Yasodhara (wife of Prince Siddhartha). Archaeological excavations feature Kanyamai temple, Bhabanipur ruins, and the ancient Rohini river boundary.

entry_fees.notes: Free public archaeological park.

name: Thame Monastery (Dechen Chokhorling)
description: Historic 17th-century monastery perched high on a granite cliff above the Bhote Koshi valley in western Khumbu. Guarding the ancient yak caravan route to Tibet via Nangpa La pass, Thame is the ancestral home of Tenzing Norgay and Apa Sherpa. The monastery preserves rare Nyingma relics and hosts dramatic masked Cham dances during the annual Dumji and Mani Rimdu festivals.

entry_fees.notes: Monastery preservation donation. Requires Sagarmatha National Park Permit and Khumbu Entry Card.

must_try: Hike up the cliff trail from Thame village to explore the rebuilt prayer hall and gaze across the valley toward the snowy ridge of Kongde Ri.
accessibility: High mountain trekking trail (~3 hours walk from Namche Bazaar).

name: Khumjung Monastery (Yeti Scalp Gompa)
description: Central village monastery of Khumjung, the largest Sherpa settlement in Khumbu, nestled in a high amphitheater beneath the sacred peak of Mount Khumbila. name: Ghar Gompa (Lo Gekar Monastery)
description: One of the oldest functioning Nyingma monasteries in the Himalayas, founded in the 8th century by Guru Padmasambhava. According to sacred Tibetan chronicles, Guru Rinpoche was called to Tibet to build Samye Monastery, but demons kept tearing down the construction; he traveled to Lo Gekar to defeat a formidable demoness, burying her heart at this site, after which Samye was successfully completed. Houses hundreds of painted stone relief carvings of deities and saints.

entry_fees.notes: Village monastery donation. Upper Mustang RAP + ACAP required.

guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Open to permitted travelers.

name: Chhoser Sky Caves (Shija Jhong Cave)
description: Prehistoric multi-storied cliff cave complex carved into vertical red bluffs north of Lo Manthang near the Tibetan border. Shija Jhong Cave rises five stories high inside the cliff face, featuring over 40 interconnected carved chambers, wooden ladders, sleeping platforms, grain storage niches, and defensive arrow slits dating back more than 2,500 years.

guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Open to permitted visitors.

name: Milarepa Cave (Ladar, Manang)
description: Sacred meditation cave perched at 4,100m on the rugged southern slopes above the Annapurna Circuit trail near Braka. Consecrated in the 11th century by the legendary Tibetan yogi-poet Jetsun Milarepa during his mountain retreat. Here, according to Buddhist lore, Milarepa converted the hunter Chirawa Gonpo Dorje after miraculously pacifying the hunter's fierce dog and a terrified hunted deer.

entry_fees.notes: Free pilgrimage cave shrine; small donation box inside. ACAP permit required.

guidelines.dress_code: Alpine trekking gear; remove boots before stepping onto the small cave shrine mat.
guidelines.sanctum_restrictions: Open to all respectful trekkers and pilgrims.
guidelines.photography: Permitted in the outer meadow and cave entrance.

must_try: Undertake the strenuous 3-hour acclimatization day-hike from Braka to the cave, enjoying the dramatic view of Annapurna III and its hanging glacier.
accessibility: Strenuous uphill mountain trail ascending from 3,450m to 4,100m.

name: Chiwong Monastery
description: Perched on a high cliff surrounded by pine and rhododendron forests above Phaplu in Solu, Chiwong Monastery was established in 1923 by Sangey Lama.
